project.name: Kiwiplan MES (Java 11 → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 modernization)
project.description:
Reference Java 11 → Java 21 LTS modernization scaffold for a Kiwiplan MES work-order slice, from a signed java spec (spec/v1, schemaId=java, targetStack=java-spring). This is an IN-PLACE upgrade, not a cross-language migration — so the scaffold shows the MODERNIZED Java 21 forms: * a verbose POJO ⟶ a record (Dimensions) * a status enum/int + if-else ⟶ a sealed interface + pattern-matching switch (WorkOrderState / WorkOrderStateMachine) * new Date(y-1900,m-1,d) / new Integer(int) ⟶ java.time.LocalDate / Integer.valueOf (ShipmentScheduler) * collect(Collectors.toList()) that is later mutated ⟶ a MUTABLE copy of Stream.toList() (BatchPlanner) — the unmodifiable-toList edge case * multi-line string concatenation ⟶ a text block (PricingReport)
The framework-level upgrades (javax.* ⟶ jakarta.*, WebSecurityConfigurer- Adapter ⟶ SecurityFilterChain) CANNOT be compiled offline (no Spring/ jakarta in the maven-sidecar cache), so they are documented @Modernization contracts (SecurityConfigContract) rather than stubbed live wiring. The Java 21 LANGUAGE modernizations ARE real code the JUnit suite verifies — the whole point is that behaviour is preserved across the upgrade, so the invariants are the contract.
Builds OFFLINE on the maven-sidecar's JDK 21 (pinned plugins + junit/ assertj). Source AND target are Java, so source-execution equivalence is feasible in principle, but is not wired; the golden extraction score + this suite are the gates.
